title: Beginner’s Guide to Your First Places Space
steps: Build a small world you can explore.
Start with an empty project. Enclose a Backrooms room, furnish it, then link it by elevator to a Home room and a Pool room.
Along the way you will make walls, an open doorway, doors, pillars, lights, furniture and water.

For Places 0.13.1.
No previous editor experience needed. No entities or Luau required.
intro: A practical, illustrated walkthrough • native macOS editor captures • keyboard equivalents for Windows
note: Keep this PDF beside the editor. Work through the numbered pages in order; save at each checkpoint.
caption: Actual native Places 0.13.1 editor capture.

title: 01  Plan your three rooms
steps: One level, three rooms, three linked elevator cabins. The rooms sit side by side on the same floor. The elevator makes them feel like separate destinations; no extra project levels or scripts are needed.
A room supplies a floor and ceiling. It does not supply walls. You will build the enclosing walls explicitly, then add interior partitions.

Metres: X runs left/right, Z runs across the floor, and Y is height. Room and wall X/Z values locate their minimum corner. Props use their placement origin. Keep floors at Y = 0 and ceilings at 2.7 m.
The route: Backrooms → elevator → Home → elevator → Pool → elevator → Backrooms. The pool is shallow; the duck sits on its bench.
table: Desk, chair, three pillars, open doorway
Shallow basin, bench, duck, janitor closet
note: Leave the gaps between rooms empty. The elevator cabins occupy space behind each room’s south wall.

title: 02  Start a new project
steps: 1. Open places-editor (Windows: places-editor.exe). Keep the installation’s assets folder and compiler in their supplied locations.
2. Click New. Choose a writable parent folder, such as Documents. The editor creates a new child project inside it.
3. The starter is a 6 × 6 m room with one ceiling light and no walls. Its spawn is at X 3, Z 4.5.
4. Click Save. Keep the whole project folder; its JSON source is what you edit.
note: You should see a square floor, a ceiling fixture and the Build / Assets / Lighting tabs. If you cannot see the room, press F to frame it.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 03  Learn the view and number fields
steps: Move the view: right-drag orbits; middle-drag pans; the wheel zooms. Hold right mouse and W/A/S/D to fly; Q/E moves down/up.
Select: click an object. Its outline and properties appear. Press F or click Frame to centre it. Scene opens a searchable list.
Enter a value: click the field, press Cmd+A on Mac or Ctrl+A on Windows, type, then Enter.
Precise edits: Exact transform opens all pose fields. Preview shows the result; Apply pose commits it. Escape cancels a draft.
note: Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes a completed edit. Cmd/Ctrl+S saves. Do not rely on the apparent screen distance: use the supplied numeric values.
caption: Actual native Places 0.13.1 editor capture.

title: 04  Find the wall tools
steps: 1. Click Tools > in the top bar.
2. Choose Geometry / stairs >. Then choose Wall: enter coordinates > at the bottom of that sheet.
3. This guide uses numeric walls so every room and doorway can be reproduced exactly.
For freehand work later: Build > Wall starts a wall on a floor click. A second click ends it. Chain continues connected segments; Escape stops.
note: The numeric form is titled Wall / numeric placement. It has X, Z, two extents, base Y and height. The next page gives the first four walls.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Inside Geometry / stairs
Choose Wall: enter coordinates to open the six-field form on the next page.

title: 05  Enclose the Backrooms room
steps: 1. Fill the first row of the table below. Leave World base Y = 0 and Height blank so the wall follows the ceiling.
2. Click Preview, then Apply. The wall becomes part of your scene.
3. Reopen Tools > Geometry / stairs > Wall: enter coordinates for each remaining row. Each opening of that command creates a new wall.
4. Leave the second-page material blank here: the default is the yellow Backrooms wallpaper. Save.
note: Four walls meet without overlapping corners. Looking down hides the ceiling so you can inspect the inside.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 06  Make an open doorway
steps: 1. Add one more numeric wall: X 0.2, Z 3.6, X extent 5.6, Z extent 0.2. Keep base Y 0 and height blank.
2. This partition splits the room into a furnished area and a small elevator lobby.
3. Choose Build > Doorway opening. Point at the partition near its centre, X 3. You should see an opening preview.
4. Click to cut the opening. This makes an open passage; no door leaf is added. Save.
note: Check that you can see through the partition. An opening belongs to its wall: do not delete the wall to make a doorway.
caption: Doorway preview on the partition. This reference view already includes furniture added in later steps.
detail_text:
Control close-up
This is a magnified crop of the same native screenshot. Match the tab and command label before clicking.

title: 07  Add three pillars
steps: 1. Open Tools > Geometry / stairs > Rectangular pillar.
2. Enter X 1.5, Z 2.5, Width 0.4, Depth 0.4. Leave Base Y and Height blank: the pillar spans floor to ceiling.
3. Click Preview, then Apply. Reopen Rectangular pillar to create the second one.
4. Repeat at X 4.1, Z 2.5, then at X 1.5, Z 1. Use the same 0.4 × 0.4 m footprint for all three. Save.
note: There is a clear centre route between the three pillars and through the doorway. Keep that path free of furniture.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 08a  Choose a furnishing prop
steps: 1. Click an empty patch of room floor to clear any prop selection.
2. Open the Assets tab, then choose Props. The search box now filters models.
3. Click the search box. Press Cmd/Ctrl+A, type core:desk, then Enter. Click the matching tile.
4. Click Place chosen prop. It appears near your view target. Use the next page to set its exact position.
caption: Magnified native catalog view. The captured example has core:chair selected; use core:desk first.
note: Do not click a new model tile while another prop is selected unless you intend to replace that prop. Select clear floor first.

title: 08b  Place the desk and chair
steps: 1. From above, click empty floor. Open Assets, choose Props, and search for core:desk. Click its tile, then Place chosen prop.
2. The new prop appears near the view target. With it selected, click Exact transform >. Enter the desk values below, Preview, then Apply pose.
3. Click empty floor again before searching for core:chair. Place it and enter the chair values.
Important: choosing a model while a prop is selected replaces that prop. Selecting floor first protects your existing furniture.
note: Keep Pitch and Roll at 0. Prop Y is above the supporting floor; ordinary floor furniture uses Y = 0.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 09  Light the Backrooms lobby
steps: 1. The starter light already illuminates the furnished side. Add a second fixture for the space behind the partition.
2. Click the Lighting tab, then Place light fixture. Point at the lobby floor near X 3, Z 4.6.
3. The preview places a real fixture at the ceiling above that floor point. Click to place it; Escape cancels an unfinished placement.
4. Select it to inspect its power, range and colour. Keep the defaults for now, then Save.
note: Inspect view uses neutral editing light. Test in editor uses approximate lighting; the final build computes the finished lighting and shadows.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Control close-up
This is a magnified crop of the same native screenshot. Match the tab and command label before clicking.

title: 10  Create the Home room
steps: 1. Choose Build > Room. In the room form enter West X 10, North Z 0, Width 6, Depth 6, Floor elevation 0 and Room height 2.7.
2. Click Preview, then Apply. This is a new floor and ceiling, with no automatic walls.
3. Enclose it using the four numeric wall rows below. Base Y stays 0; Height stays blank.
4. For each wall click Page > and set its material to home:wall_paint_offwhite_01 before Preview / Apply.
note: Both rooms have the same floor elevation. Their four-metre separation leaves room for independent enclosure.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 11  Give Home its own surfaces
steps: 1. Orbit to a steep overhead view. Click clear floor inside Home. Confirm the properties describe a Room, not a wall or prop.
2. Choose Assets > Surface. Search home:hardwood_oak_01 and click its tile to apply it to the floor.
3. To change a ceiling, select the room, then open Tools > Surface material >. Click the Surface / Ceiling switch to choose Ceiling.
4. Search home:ceiling_white_01 and choose its tile. Reopen the picker and switch back to Surface before later floor assignments.
note: Material IDs are exact catalog search terms. If you see no results, clear the search with Cmd/Ctrl+A and check that All themes is selected.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Control close-up
This is a magnified crop of the same native screenshot. Match the tab and command label before clicking.

title: 12  Furnish the Home room
steps: 1. Repeat the Assets > Props workflow. Select empty floor before choosing each new model.
2. Use Place chosen prop, then Exact transform. Enter each row below with Scale 1, Yaw 0, Pitch 0 and Roll 0.
3. The cabinet, sink unit and cooker form a small kitchen along the north wall; the bed sits to its left.
4. Add Home’s ceiling light using the numeric fixture workflow in Step 19. Save before continuing.
note: Leave room to stand in front of the kitchen. These are static furnishing props; no interaction components are required.
caption: Actual native Places 0.13.1 editor capture.

title: 13  Fit a door in Home
steps: 1. Add a partition wall at X 10.2, Z 3.6, with X extent 5.6 and Z extent 0.2. Use Home’s wall material.
2. Choose Build > Door. Point at the centre of the partition, around X 13.
3. Inspect the preview, then click. Door creates a fitted opening and an interactive door leaf in one action.
4. Keep the initial door style. In play, press E to open, step back while it swings, then centre yourself in the opening and walk through.
note: Doorway opening (Step 6) cuts only a hole. Door adds the leaf too, and can also fit a leaf into a suitable existing doorway.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Control close-up
This is a magnified crop of the same native screenshot. Match the tab and command label before clicking.

title: 14  Build the Pool room shell
steps: 1. Build > Room: enter X 20, Z 0, Width 8, Depth 8, Floor elevation 0, Height 2.7. Preview and Apply.
2. Add the four walls below. On their second form page, set core:pool_tile_wall_01. Base Y is 0; Height is blank.
3. Select the floor and assign core:pool_tile_deck_01 through Assets > Surface.
4. Through the room’s Surface material picker, switch to Ceiling and assign core:pool_ceiling_01. Switch back to Surface afterwards.
note: Keep the room floor at Y = 0. The next step lowers only the basin area.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 15  Recess the shallow pool basin
steps: 1. Open Tools > Environment / space >, then GLOBAL surface region.
2. Enter X 21.5, Z 2, Width 3, Depth 3. Set Offset on ALL carriers = -0.4.
3. Set Surface material ID to core:pool_tile_basin_01. On Page >, set Edge material ID to the same value.
4. Preview and Apply. The basin is now 40 cm below the deck. This operation changes solid floor geometry; it does not add water.
note: This deliberately shallow basin stays within the player’s 0.45 m step allowance. Global regions affect overlapping floor carriers, so do not stack another room over this tutorial basin.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Inside Environment / space
Choose GLOBAL surface region. This edits the floor geometry beneath the water.

title: 16  Fill the basin with water
steps: 1. Open Tools > Environment / space > Water volume.
2. Match the basin: X 21.5, Z 2, Width 3, Depth 3.
3. Set World surface Y = -0.1 and World bottom Y = -0.4. Keep the remaining default settings.
4. Preview and Apply. The water surface sits 10 cm below the deck, with 30 cm of water above the basin floor. Save.
note: Water is separate from the solid basin. Keep its footprint inside the recess; water by itself does not make a hole or a supporting floor.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 17  Make a small janitor closet
steps: 1. Reserve the northeast corner of the Pool room. Two new walls use the existing north and east walls to enclose a closet.
2. Add the two numeric walls below with core:pool_tile_wall_01. Keep base Y 0 and Height blank.
3. Choose Build > Door. Point at the closet’s south wall near X 26.5, Z 2.8. Check the preview and click.
4. Add the fixture in Step 19. In play, open with E, step back, then centre yourself in the opening before walking in. The swing can nudge you sideways.
note: The closet uses the Pool room’s existing floor and ceiling. Do not place a second coplanar room inside it.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 18  Add the bench and rubber duck
steps: 1. Select clear floor, search pool:pool_bench in Assets > Props, and place it. Apply the bench pose below.
2. Select clear floor again, search core:rubber_duck, and place it. Use Exact transform to apply the duck pose.
3. The duck sits on the bench at Y 0.45. This is a static decoration; no floating behaviour or script is needed.
4. Save, then check the side view: bench feet touch the deck, and the duck rests on the seat.
note: Keep Pitch and Roll at 0. The duck is small at its real catalog scale; zoom in rather than enlarging it.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 19  Light Home, Pool and closet
steps: 1. Open Tools > Environment / space > Light / numeric placement. The form provides exact placement and fixture IDs.
2. Click New to add a fixture. Enter the first row below. Leave World ceiling Y blank for automatic ceiling mounting. Set Power to 1; leave Range blank.
3. Preview and Apply. To add another fixture, reopen the form and choose New before entering the next row.
4. Repeat for the Pool room and closet, then Save. Each enclosed area now has a fixture.
note: Leave Alignment at none and Yaw at 0. A decorative lamp model is not a substitute for a placed light fixture.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 20  Place three elevator cabins
steps: 1. Go inside the Backrooms lobby and face its south wall. Choose Build > Elevator.
2. Point near X 3, Z 5.8 on that wall. The preview fits the cabin and opening to the actual wall face. Click to place.
3. In the elevator sheet choose Name, type Backrooms and press Enter. Close the sheet.
4. Repeat in Home at X 13, Z 5.8 and Pool at X 24, Z 7.8. Name those stops Home and Pool.
note: Place from the room side so the cabin extends behind the wall. The fitted opening is 1.50 × 2.25 m. Keep each cabin’s doorway and the space behind the wall clear.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.
detail_text:
Control close-up
This is a magnified crop of the same native screenshot. Match the tab and command label before clicking.

title: 21  Link the elevator destinations
steps: 1. Choose Build > Elevator, then click the Backrooms cabin to open its sheet. Choose Link selected, move to Home, and click Home’s cabin.
2. The connection is bidirectional. In the cabin sheet, select Backrooms from the cabin list and choose Link selected again.
3. Click the Pool cabin. The group now contains all three stops; each cabin has the other two as destinations.
4. Save. Reopen the project later to confirm the links persist. Do not add a fourth cabin to this group.
note: The current linked group supports three cabins. These three rooms share one level, so no Allowed transitions list or cross-level destination setup is needed.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 22  Save and test your space
steps: 1. Click Save or press Cmd/Ctrl+S. Then click Test in editor to start at the authored spawn.
2. Walk through the open Backrooms doorway. Check the chair and pillars do not block your route.
3. Test Home’s door and the closet door with E. Check the pool edge and bench placement. Use Here > a floor pick to start a separate local test near another room if needed.
4. Press Escape to stop and return to editing. Quick testing is temporary; it does not save source or bake final lighting.
table: E use / pick up / drop; F flashlight
Left click throws a held item
note: Use the exported player build for the final elevator round trip. Quick tests are useful for local collision and door checks, not proof of final lighting.
caption: Actual native Places 0.13.1 editor capture.

title: 23  Compile and export
steps: 1. Stop testing. Click Final build. It saves dirty levels and compiles the selected level with production lighting.
2. Wait for success. The progress bar describes the current pass, not the whole job. Fix any reported error before continuing.
3. Open Project > Export all levels + sources. Enter a full, absolute file path ending in .placesmap in a writable folder.
4. Apply and wait for successful export. Keep the editable project folder too. Source saves and compiled packages serve different purposes.
note: Example on Mac: /Users/your-name/Documents/first-space.placesmap. On Windows: C:/Users/your-name/Documents/first-space.placesmap. Replace your-name with your account folder.
caption: Native Places 0.13.1 editor. Red circles and arrows mark the controls named in the steps.

title: 24  Play the finished route
steps: 1. Open Places. In Explore, import your exported .placesmap, select it, then Play.
2. Walk into the Backrooms cabin. Aim at the destination control and press E or left click. Choose Home.
3. Let the doors close and the ride finish. Visit the bed and kitchen, then use Home’s cabin to reach Pool.
4. Enter the closet, walk into and out of the shallow basin, inspect the duck, then ride back to Backrooms. Try all return directions.
note: The separate green door-arrow button opens/closes doors at the current stop; it does not choose a destination. Clear the doorway if it keeps reopening.
caption: The compiled tutorial in the player: elevator destination buttons inside the cabin.

title: 25  Compare your finished Pool room

shots.caption: Standing in the shallow basin. The deck remains above the water.

shots.name: 47-duck-bench
shots.caption: The small rubber duck rests on the bench seat at Y = 0.45.

steps: Pool: your basin should be visibly recessed, with water below the deck. The 0.4 m drop lets the player walk back out.
Furniture: keep the bench on the deck and the duck on the seat. The duck is a static decorative prop in this tutorial.
Closet: open the door, give it space to swing, then align with the centre of the gap. Check that its ceiling light illuminates the interior.
note: These are actual player captures from the compiled tutorial package. Editor inspect lighting will look different.

title: 26  Your final checks and next steps
steps: Geometry: every room has four enclosing walls. The Backrooms passage is an opening without a leaf. Home and the janitor closet have usable doors. No double floors or flickering surfaces.
Placement: the desk, chair, bed and kitchen stand on the floor. The pillars leave a walkable centre route. The bench is grounded, with the duck on its seat.
Lighting and water: each enclosed area has a fixture. Water stays inside the recessed basin. Inspect the finished compiled result, then adjust and rebuild if needed.
Travel and files: all three cabin names and return routes work. Save the project, export a fresh package after changes, and retain a backup of the entire editable folder.

If something goes wrong: Escape cancels the current tool; Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes the last edit. Check the footer’s message. If a material changes the wrong object, Undo, select clear floor or the correct wall, and try again.

Continue learning: docs/EDITOR.md covers editor tools; docs/MAP_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md explains geometry and lighting; docs/ELEVATORS.md explains cabin limits. The companion editor-guide folder retains this guide’s editable source and original screenshots.
note: This walkthrough is scoped to the 0.13.1 native editor. Exact screenshots and validation details are recorded in editor-guide/README.md.
